title: Mandatory Signs vs Information Signs
whatItIs: Blue circles mostly give orders you must follow. Most blue rectangles give information, but the rectangular one-way traffic sign is also an order.
keyFacts: Blue circles with no red border mostly tell you what you must do.
Ahead only, turn left and keep left are orders, not suggestions.

keyFacts.text: The blue rectangular one-way traffic sign is an order: traffic MUST travel in the direction it shows.

keyFacts: The mini-roundabout sign is a blue circle: give way to traffic from your right.
Some blue circles show who may use a route, such as pedal cycles only.

visual.caption: Blue circles give orders; blue rectangles can order or inform

b.label: One-way traffic (rectangle)
points: The whole road carries one-way traffic
Traffic MUST go the way shown (Rule 143)

onTheTest.question: What does a blue circle with a white arrow pointing left mean?
onTheTest.why: Blue circles give orders: the arrow is the direction you must take. 'No left turn' is a red ring.

traps: Most blue rectangles inform, but not all: the rectangular one-way traffic sign is an order, just like a blue circle.
The mini-roundabout sign is a blue circle, not a warning triangle.
Keep left is an order, not advice. With the arrow reversed, the same sign means keep right.

review.checkedAgainst: Official text on gov.uk — The Highway Code: Traffic signs: signs giving orders; Know Your Traffic Signs (DfT): Regulatory signs; The Highway Code: Rule 143 (One-way streets)
